outcome: Sexual function (measured using the Female Sexual Function Index)
cohort: The study included 165 women, with 88 in the vaginal delivery group and 77 in the cesarean delivery group.
finding: While vaginal delivery was associated with lower intravaginal pressure and shorter coitus time compared to cesarean delivery, there was no significant difference in sexual satisfaction or overall sexual function between the two groups.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with lower intravaginal pressure and shorter coitus time compared to cesarean delivery, but did not negatively affect postnatal sexual function.
